rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures
rawCommits.body:
The published Windows installer was silently failing to launch on
upgraded machines. Symptom: double-click AURA, the harness sidecar
(aura-node-...) appears as a Background process in Task Manager,
and then nothing — no window, no error dialog, no notification.
Only `<localdata>/aura/crash.log` showed evidence of what happened:

  panicked at apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs:106:10:
  server thread failed before becoming ready: RecvError

Root cause is a chain of three bugs that combine into "exits
silently with no UI":

1. `<localdata>/aura/store/settings.json` was a 1.1 MB file of
   pure NUL bytes — a torn-write artifact from a prior crash.
   `SettingsStore::load_cf` handed the bytes to
   `serde_json::from_str`, which propagated `expected value at
   line 1 column 1` straight up. The same store path is read in
   two places: `init_script::load_bootstrapped_auth_literals`
   already swallowed the error and warned, but the
   server-thread path inside `aura-os-desktop` `.expect(...)`'d
   on it and panicked.
2. `persist_cf` wrote the tmp file with `fs::write` and renamed
   it without `sync_all`. NTFS happily renames a file whose
   contents the OS has not yet flushed; a power loss or hard
   kill in that window leaves the destination as the right
   length but full of NUL bytes, which is exactly the input
   that bug 1 chokes on the next time around.
3. The release Windows binary is built with
   `windows_subsystem = "windows"`, so the panic's `eprintln!`
   went to a stderr that has no console. The only surviving
   evidence was `crash.log`, which a non-developer user has no
   reason to look at.

Fixes:

- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::load_cf`: on
  `serde_json::from_str` failure, rename the bad file aside
  to `<cf>.json.corrupt-<unix_ts>`, log a WARN, and return an
  empty CF. Mirrors the per-entry tolerance the same function
  already applies to invalid base64. Two new integration tests
  cover the all-NUL and garbage-JSON shapes.
- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::persist_cf`: replace
  `fs::write` with `OpenOptions::open` + `write_all` + a
  `sync_all` before the rename so the atomic-rename promise
  actually holds across crashes. Costs one fsync per persist.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/net/server.rs::spawn_server`:
  change the ready channel from `()` to `Result<(), String>`
  and stop `.expect`ing on `build_app_state` /
  `TcpListener::from_std`. On failure, log the error and send
  `Err(message)` back so the main thread can react.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs`: handle the new ready
  result. On `Ok(Err(_))` or `RecvError`, call a new
  `init::fatal_dialog::show_fatal_startup_failure` helper
  before exiting non-zero.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/init/fatal_dialog.rs` (new): pop
  a native MessageBoxW with MB_TOPMOST + MB_SETFOREGROUND on
  Windows; fall back to `eprintln!` on macOS / Linux. The
  dialog body names the data dir, the path of the crash log,
  and the corrupt settings file the user can rename to recover.

Verified locally: `cargo test -p aura-os-store` (7 tests, both
new self-heal cases included) and
`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop -- --print-channel` (Channel CI
gate from f64e07753 still passes).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures

rawCommits.subject: fix(memory): read by bare template id, not partition key
rawCommits.body:
The May 7 fix routed memory reads through `${agent_id}::default`,
but the harness keys long-term memory by the bare template id (via
`Session::memory_agent_id`, which derives an `AgentId` from the
billing `aura_agent_id` UUID). Its router's `parse_agent_id` only
accepts UUID / 32-byte hex, so every partitioned memory request
returned 400 and the UI fell back to "no memories yet".

restore the strongly-typed `Path<AgentId>` extractors so a malformed
caller fails at the proxy edge instead of being forwarded as a bad
string, and drop the partition-shaped tests that asserted the wrong
contract (the mock harness happily echoed the partition key while
the real harness was rejecting it).

rawCommits.subject: fix(mode-selector): equal-width segments to stop pill border jitter
rawCommits.body:
The SlidingPills indicator transitions transform, width and height
together when the active mode changes. transform runs on a composited
layer but width / height force a CPU layout + paint each frame, so the
1px accent border lands at slightly different sub-pixel positions on
intermediate frames and reads as a small wobble on the pill outline
during the slide.

Pin every mode segment to the same min-width (56px desktop, 68px on
the mobile breakpoint, both border-box so the value covers padding) so
every segment measures identically. The width / height transitions
then become no-ops on mode changes and only transform actually
animates, which is fully GPU-composited and pixel-stable.

SlidingPills itself is left untouched so any future consumer that
genuinely needs unequal segment widths still gets the size transition.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(agents-chat): decouple wire project_id from picker selection
rawCommits.body:
Introduces an `llmProjectId` prop on `ChatPanel` (forwarded through
`useChatPanelState` as `wireProjectId`) that drives `body.project_id`
on the wire, separately from `selectedProjectId` which still anchors
the picker label and chat-persistence target. Defaults to
`selectedProjectId` so existing callers (projects-app via
`AgentChatPanel`, which now passes `llmProjectId={projectId}`
explicitly) keep their current behavior.

The agents-app side (`useStandaloneAgentChat`) computes
`llmProjectId` so:
- new sessions / fresh canvas / context reset always ship Home;
- existing sessions opened via `/agents/:agentId?session=<id>` ship
  the session-of-record's original project, recovered from
  `sessions-list-store` via the new `findSessionProjectId` helper —
  even when the user lands from a row unrelated to today's selected
  display project;
- legacy agents with no Home binding ship `undefined` and let the
  server's lazy heal in
  `setup_agent_chat_persistence_with_matched` create the binding on
  first turn. A heal-refresh effect then nudges
  `useProjectsListStore.refreshProjects` so the freshly-created Home
  row materializes locally for subsequent sends instead of waiting
  for a hard reload.

Test updates wire matching mocks for
`useProjectsListStore.refreshProjects`,
`useSessionsListStore.{sessionsBySurface, replaceSessionId,
bumpVersion, addOptimisticSession}`,
`agentSessionsSurfaceKey` / `projectSessionsSurfaceKey`, and a
minimal `buildOptimisticSession` shape.

rawCommits.subject: fix(ide): share main webview WebContext so IDE window inherits auth
rawCommits.body:
The IDE window was opened with a fresh isolated WebContext, so its
localStorage started empty and the per-window init-script bootstrap that
seeded `aura-jwt` / `aura-session` / `__AURA_BOOT_AUTH__` was not landing
reliably on Windows WebView2. The frontend's `getStoredJwt()` then
returned null, `authHeaders()` was empty, and every API call (file
listing, file read) hit the server's auth guard with "missing
authorization token" — the file tree showed "Could not load files" and
the editor body rendered `ApiClientError: missing authorization token`.

Switch `open_ide_window` to take the parent's `&mut WebContext` and
build via `WebViewBuilder::new_with_web_context`, mirroring how
`open_secondary_main_window` already shares storage with the primary
window. With localStorage shared, the IDE inherits the live session
directly, no per-window auth bake-in needed, and login/logout in any
window propagates to the others through the same web storage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: share main webview WebContext so IDE window inherits auth

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): add @-mention file autocomplete to input bar
rawCommits.body:
Typing `@` in a project-scoped chat now opens an autocomplete menu
of the project's files (mirrors the existing `/` slash-command
trigger). Selecting a file strips the `@query` token and pushes
the file through the existing attachment pipeline, with the S3
upload running in the background just like a drag/drop attach.

Standalone (project-less) chats leave the menu dormant — the
`workspacePath` resolved by `useTerminalTarget` gates activation,
so the trigger is silent when there's no workspace to resolve
files against.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): register @-mention attachment synchronously to block premature send
rawCommits.body:
`addFileFromPath` was async — fetching the file via `api.readFile`
before registering the attachment in state. A user who typed
`@foo`, hit Enter to pick the file, then hit Enter again to send
would race the file read: the second Enter fired `handleSend`
while `attachments` was still empty, the message went out without
the file, and the agent only saw the bare prompt.

Push a placeholder `AttachmentItem` (uploading=true, empty data)
synchronously BEFORE the API read so the chip appears immediately
AND `isUploading` flips true — which the input bar already wires
into `disabled`, blocking Enter until the upload finishes. After
the file content arrives we replace the placeholder in place
(same id) and kick the existing S3 upload pipeline. Mirrors the
synchronous-then-upload contract `addFiles` already provides via
FileReader for drag/drop + paste flows.

Failed reads drop the placeholder so the user isn't stuck with a
phantom chip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): persist unsent prompt drafts across session/route switches
rawCommits.body:
Lift the chat input's draft text out of `useChatPanelState`'s local
`useState` into a new per-`streamKey` slot in `chat-ui-store.drafts`.
Switching sessions or navigating away and back now restores the
typed-but-unsent text for that chat. Attachments and slash-command

so the store contains exactly "chats with currently-typed-but-unsent

automatically, and backspacing to empty drops them too. State is

rawCommits.subject: fix(agents-chat): clear `?project=` / `?instance=` alongside `?session=` on reset
rawCommits.body:
The standalone default-session redirect at `/agents/:agentId` writes
the full URL triple (`?project=`, `?instance=`, `?session=`) so a cold
open snaps to the most-recent session. The "+" and RotateCcw paths
only cleared `?session=`, leaving the `?project=` / `?instance=`
mirrors behind — which the conversation-target resolver (step 3) read
as a deep-link back into `AgentChatPanel` for the legacy binding (e.g.
"zero-sdk-10") even after the user explicitly asked for a fresh
canvas. Result: the project picker stayed pinned to the legacy
project name instead of flipping to "Home", and the LLM input shipped
that legacy id as `body.project_id`, undoing the previous decoupling
refactor for any agent whose default-session redirect had ever fired.

Both writers (`useFreshCanvas.dropSessionParam` for the project /
step-4 resolution path, and `useStandaloneAgentChat`'s
`handleNewSession` / `handleNewChat` for the standalone path) now drop
all three keys together. In the projects route the path carries the
binding so the query mirrors are redundant — dropping them there is a
safe no-op.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-input): stop mode-selector pill from sliding on app switch
rawCommits.body:
Suppress the SlidingPills indicator transition for non-user-driven
applies (initial mount + ResizeObserver callbacks). The CSS rule
defaults `transform: translate(0, 0)` and declares 140ms transitions
on transform/width/height, so remounting ModeSelector when the user
switched apps slid the indicator from the origin into the active
segment, and post-mount layout settling (centered -> bottom reveal,
scrollbar, font swap) re-triggered slides. Only animate when the
controlled `value` actually changes between renders; otherwise write
`transition: none`, set geometry, flush via `offsetWidth`, then
restore the cascaded transition for future user clicks.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): clip generated-image wrappers so the rounded border isn't notched at the corners
rawCommits.body: `.generatedImageLink` and `.mediaImageButton` paint a 1px rounded frame around LLM-generated s in assistant turns, but neither clipped its child. The inner image's square corners poked past the wrapper's rounded arcs and visually punched out the border at each corner. Adding `overflow: hidden` keeps the rounded frame intact regardless of the rendered image's aspect-ratio. Also gives `.mediaImage` a matching `border-radius: 4px` (and `display: block`) so its own 1px border isn't a sharp-cornered rectangle inside an otherwise rounded layout. Co-authored-by: Cursor

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-sessions): restore + new-chat by keeping panel mounted on agents-shell
rawCommits.body:
Commit f28e2c62a started clearing `?project=` / `?instance=` alongside
`?session=` from `useFreshCanvas.dropSessionParam` and the standalone
`handleNewSession` / `handleNewChat`. On the agents-shell route
(`/agents/:agentId`) that flipped `useConversationTarget` from `ready`
to `empty`, swapping `AgentChatPanel` -> `StandaloneAgentChatPanel`
mid-press. Two regressions followed:

- The just-armed optimistic "New chat" row from
  `useOptimisticSessionRow.arm()` was yanked by the hook's unmount
  cleanup, so the sidekick never showed the new entry.
- `StandaloneAgentChatPanel` mounted with `freshCanvasPending=false`
  and re-fetched `api.agents.listEvents`, so the transcript visibly
  re-populated with the agent's full timeline instead of clearing.

Drop only `?session=` from all three writers so the agents-shell
panel stays mounted on the same `(project, instance)` lane with
`sessionId=null`. The panel's existing `freshCanvasPending` plumbing
(history key flips to `fresh:...:nonce`, `fetchFn` short-circuits to
`EMPTY_SESSION_EVENTS_FETCH`) takes over and clears the transcript;
`useOptimisticSessionRow.arm()` keeps the row visible.

Defensive change in `useConversationTarget` step 3: when
`userClearedSession` is true and the query mirrors are missing (stale
tab, deep-link share, external navigator), fall through to the agent's
most-recent binding instead of returning `kind: "empty"`. This keeps
`AgentChatPanel` mounted in those edge cases too, so the optimistic
row still survives if the user takes the "+" path from there.

Trade-off: the picker label / wire `body.project_id` for legacy agents
on a fresh canvas now show the legacy project again, exactly as they
did before f28e2c62a. The cleanup belongs in a dedicated agents-shell-aware
picker/wire override on `AgentChatPanel`, not in a URL clear that breaks
the row-survival contract.

Tests:
- `AgentChatRoute.test.tsx` regression for the realistic post-`+`
  URL state (`?session=` removed, mirrors retained) — expects
  `agent-chat-panel` (not `standalone-agent-chat-panel`) with
  `sessionId=null`.
- Defensive coverage for the no-query-mirrors case where
  `mostRecentStandalone` keeps the panel mounted on its binding.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: AURA Video launches, Windows startup self-heal, and chat input overhaul
rendered.intro: A heavy day across the stack: a brand-new AURA Video app lands end-to-end, the Windows desktop client gains a self-healing settings store and a real "could not start" dialog, and the chat input bar picks up @-mention file context, persistent drafts, and a long sweep of pixel-level polish. Release pipelines also got tougher against flaky GitHub uploads and Apple notary outages.

entries.title: @-mention file context, persistent drafts, and feedback authoring
entries.summary: Chat picks up file autocomplete and draft persistence, while the feedback sidekick gains inline comments and author-controlled status changes.

items.text: Typing @ in a project-scoped chat now opens a file autocomplete that attaches the picked file through the same S3 upload pipeline as drag-and-drop, with a synchronous placeholder chip so a fast double-Enter no longer races the file read and sends the message empty.

Unsent chat prompts now persist per session in the chat UI store, so switching sessions or navigating away and back restores the text you were typing (attachments and slash chips still reset with the session).

The feedback Details tab now shows an inline newest-first comment list, and submitting authors can change Status directly from a scoped dropdown (current → Not Started / Done / Deployed) to close their own items in one click.

Added an Invite Friends modal triggered from a new pulsing taskbar button, and introduced separate border tokens so users can tint the desktop lane borders independently from the topbar and taskbar chrome in Settings → Appearance.
Fixed a Windows-only IDE window auth bug by sharing the main webview's WebContext, so the IDE inherits the live session instead of rendering 'missing authorization token' for every file API call.

entries.title: Self-healing release uploads via reconcile-and-retry
entries.summary: Release jobs no longer fail outright when GitHub drops a single asset upload mid-flight.

items.text: Added a reconcile script that diffs local artifacts against the published release and re-uploads only missing or wrong-sized assets with retries on transient EPIPE / ECONNRESET / 'other side closed' errors. Wired into every release flow (immutable nightly, nightly alias, stable, mobile-nightly) so a single dropped softprops upload no longer reds an entire 40-minute pipeline.

entries.title: Unified sidekick width and cleaner desktop lane shaping
entries.summary: The desktop shell simplifies sidekick sizing and tightens the visual treatment of its main lanes.

items.text: The sidekick lane now uses a single shared width across every app instead of per-app persistence and on-switch retargeting, with a one-time migration from the legacy keys so existing users keep their preferred size.

Replaced the inset divider against the sidekick with explicit rounded corners on the sidebar, main panel host, and sidekick lane, with the main panel only rounding its right edge when the sidekick is collapsed.
Empty-chat prompt suggestions now appear only during onboarding and disappear the moment a user sends their first-ever message.

entries.title: AURA Video app and a no-more-silent-exit Windows fix
entries.summary: A new end-to-end video generation app lands alongside a major Windows reliability fix and a wave of taskbar and sidebar polish.

items.text: Shipped AURA Video as a standalone app: Veo Fast/Standard/Lite models, a /api/generate/video/stream proxy reusing the harness pipeline, a Zustand-backed store, prompt input with model picker and progress UI, a left-nav project tree, and a sidekick gallery with thumbnail grid and context-menu delete.

Fixed Windows installs that launched silently after a torn settings.json write: the store now quarantines corrupt files and returns an empty CF, persist now fsyncs before rename so atomic-rename actually holds across crashes, and a fatal startup failure now pops a native 'AURA could not start' dialog pointing at the crash log instead of vanishing into the windowed subsystem.
Restored agent memory loading by reverting reads to the bare template id the harness keys on, with strongly-typed extractors that reject malformed ids at the proxy edge instead of forwarding 400s.

Reworked the bottom taskbar: collapsed the right cluster to a profile-only default behind a chevron, moved the day/night theme toggle into the taskbar pills next to Help, and iterated the Earn Credits / Invite CTAs through several placements before landing the EARN pill in the titlebar action row.

Polished the mode selector and sidebar highlights: equal-width segments stop the active pill's border from jittering during slides, the selected segment now fills with accent + contrast text, the redundant MODE label is gone, and sidebar/sidekick row highlights share a single inset pill style.

entries.title: Mac packaging retries on Apple notary outages
entries.summary: Transient Apple notary failures no longer red the macOS packaging job.

items.text: Extended the desktop packaging retry matcher so xcrun notarytool HTTP 429 and 5xx responses (in addition to existing hdiutil 'Resource busy' flakes) trigger a retry instead of aborting the macOS release.

entries.title: Standalone agents chat pinned to Home, plus input bar refinement
entries.summary: Standalone agent chats get a consistent Home picker and a decoupled wire project id, while the chat input picks up a shared icon-button hover system and many alignment fixes.

items.text: Standalone Agents-app chats now always render the project picker as a single non-interactive 'Home' entry — auto-bound for new agents and synthesized for legacy bindings — and a new llmProjectId prop decouples the wire body.project_id from the picker label so fresh canvases ship Home, existing sessions ship their session-of-record's project, and legacy agents trigger a server-side lazy heal plus local refresh.

Reset paths now only drop ?session= (not the whole URL triple), keeping AgentChatPanel mounted on the agents-shell route so the optimistic 'New chat' row survives in the sidekick and the transcript clears via freshCanvasPending instead of re-fetching the full timeline.

Introduced a shared inner-plate icon hover treatment driven by --icon-hover-inset / --icon-hover-radius / --icon-hover-bg tokens, applied across the taskbar, app nav rail, and the input bar's attach, send, and new-chat buttons, with centering safeguards and a new icon-system.md as the source of truth.

Stopped the mode-selector pill from sliding on every app switch or post-mount layout shift by suppressing SlidingPills' transition for non-user-driven updates and only animating when the controlled value actually changes.

Tightened chat transcript and input chrome: desktop inter-message gap bumped from 2px to 8px, image-only user messages get extra bottom margin, generated-image wrappers clip their rounded frame, corner buttons share a 2px inset, the mode-bar divider spans the full row, and the Code-mode placeholder now hints '/ for commands, @ for context'.

highlights: AURA Video app shipped with Veo models, gallery, and SSE streaming
Windows installer no longer fails silently on corrupt settings
@-mention file context in chat with persistent drafts
Release pipeline survives dropped uploads and Apple notary 5xx
Standalone agents chat now pinned to a consistent Home project
